title: A negative regulator of mitochondrial complex I assembly adapts respiration to cellular energy demand
authors: Zhirong Li, Nuo Chen, Caixia Zhou, Lingna Xu, Xiyuan Wang, Hong Xu, Weina Shang, Jun-Ping Liu, Liquan Wang, Chao Tong
abstract: Li et al. identify TMEM141 as a negative regulator of mitochondrial complex I assembly. Under high energy demand, the YME1L1 and AFG3L2 proteases degrade TMEM141, relieving its inhibition of the assembly factor TIMMDC1. This work reveals a mechanism that adapts complex I assembly to OXPHOS demands.

authors: Shuhei Asada, Guangli Zhu, Jithma Prasad Abeykoon, Yutaro Tanaka, Huy Nguyen, Yuna Hirohashi, Divya R. abstract: Asada et al. show that EWS-FLI1 disrupts EWSR1-dependent POLQ pre-mRNA splicing, causing Polθ loss and MMEJ deficiency in Ewing sarcoma. This repair defect creates synthetic lethal vulnerabilities to FA, HR, and NHEJ pathway inhibition, revealing actionable therapeutic strategies.

abstract: Akçaöz-Alasar et al. reveal that the mitotic kinase CDK1 phosphorylates the m6A methyltransferase METTL3, which then methylates 7SK RNA to release P-TEFb and promote RNA polymerase II clearance during mitosis, ensuring proper chromosome segregation.

title: α-Satellite RNA maintains centromeric cohesion through R-loops
authors: Lu Yang, Qian Zhang, Zhen Teng, Erin Moran, Zhen Lin, P. Todd Stukenberg, Hong Liu
abstract: Yang et al. show that α-satellite RNA, derived from human centromeric satellite repeats, forms R-loops at human centromeres to ensure faithful chromosome segregation by recruiting Shugoshin 1. This mechanism is essential for preserving chromosomal stability.
